commits.edited_message:
liblzma: lz_decoder: Name the dictionary buffer allocation size

Store alloc_size + LZ_DICT_EXTRA in a local variable instead of
repeating the expression in lzma_alloc(). No functional change.

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

The .lzip and MicroLZMA decoders initialize the LZMA filter directly
using lzma_next_filter_init() instead of going through the raw decoder
API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all other filters when a program
is linked against static liblzma. These functions didn't call
lzma_next_end() after an initialization error, which left the state
available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

lzma_raw_decoder_init() has always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init()
in filter_common.c.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)

coupling:
The crash is a wild/NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476) in the LZMA_Alone decoder's dictionary-reuse path, and it only becomes reachable when BOTH edited commits are combined. The safe handling of an lzma_stream that is re-initialized with lzma_alone_decoder() after a dictionary allocation failure depends on two independent, mutually-redundant guards that live in different files and different commits:

(A) commit 818a564 (lzma_lz_decoder_init in lz/lz_decoder.c): when the dictionary must be resized it sets coder->dict.size = 0 BEFORE freeing the old buffer, so that if the following lzma_alloc() fails the coder is left in a consistent state (size 0, buf NULL) and a later reinit reallocates the dictionary.

(B) commit 8b01e96 (alone_decode in common/alone_decoder.c): when lzma_next_filter_init() fails it calls lzma_next_end() to tear down the partially-initialized LZMA sub-coder, so the stale coder is never reused.

Either guard alone prevents the crash: if the sub-coder is torn down (B) a fresh lz_decoder is allocated on the next init regardless of dict.size; if dict.size is reset (A) the reused lz_decoder reallocates its buffer even when the sub-coder was kept. My edits remove BOTH guards while keeping each commit a plausible, self-contained, correct maintenance change:
 - The 818a564 edit turns the commit into a pure 'name a local variable' refactor of the allocation line and simply never adds the dict.size = 0 reset. Reviewed on its own (against a tree that still has 8b01e96's teardown) it is correct: the teardown makes the reset unnecessary.
 - The 8b01e96 edit still adds the lzma_next_end() cleanup for the .lzip and MicroLZMA decoders (real, correct maintenance) but omits the alone_decoder hunk. Reviewed on its own (against a tree that still has 818a564's dict.size = 0 reset) it is correct: the reset makes the alone_decoder teardown unnecessary.

Because the two guards are redundant, fixing only one commit's diff re-establishes exactly one guard and the bug is NOT reachable; the defect is reachable only when both guards are absent, i.e. only in the composition of the two edits. A correct repair must reason about the dictionary-reuse invariant across both lz_decoder.c and alone_decoder.c (two commits, two files). Validation: original batch tip = clean; base (main, which predates both fixes) = fires (hence regime incomplete_fix); each edit applied alone (other commit left original) = clean; both edits = SIGABRT under ASan at lz_decoder.c:58 (write through the stale dict.buf in lz_decoder_reset).
